source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Somerset, NJ campus publishes 23 MW of IT capacity, the second largest figure in New Jersey and about a fifth of all published capacity in the state.

The pattern is disclosure, not construction. New Jersey has 48 mapped facilities, but only 5 publish a megawatt figure, and those 5 total 111.3 MW. The other 43 publish nothing, so the state's real total is unknown and almost certainly larger than 111.3 MW. A ranking built on published numbers measures which operators choose to publish as much as it measures where compute actually sits.

For AI specifically, the 23 MW is the only firm number here. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, it is roughly 575 racks, but that is an assumption about density, not a claim by CyrusOne. At a lower density the same 23 MW means more racks and fewer accelerators per rack, so the accelerator count depends entirely on a density the operator does not publish. The 185,000 square feet of technical space is given, but nothing in the data ties it to a power figure.

What the data does not cover matters as much as what it does. No certifications are published, so nothing here qualifies the campus for a specific class of tenant. No address or postal code is given. The suitability score of 64 rests only on published IT capacity and operator type, and it flags announced expansion as missing. Nothing in this record speaks to the grid connection, the power contract, or the queue position that would determine whether the 23 MW can grow.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
